item.title: Orpo urges Xi to help end Ukraine war during China visit
item.description: Petteri Orpo has called on Xi Jinping to use his influence to help stop Russia’s war in Ukraine. The Finnish Prime Minister made the statement during a state visit to China, where he held talks with the country’s leadership. “Xi has the power to help bring peace to Ukraine,” Orpo said during a press briefing at the Finnish Embassy in Beijing. He stated that China’s support for Russia, direct or indirect, weakens ties between China and the European Union.

item.title: Unemployment in Finland hits highest level since 2009
item.description: Unemployment in Finland rose to 10.7 percent in December 2025, marking the highest rate recorded since 2009, according to data released by Statistics Finland. The number of unemployed persons increased by 51,000 compared to the previous year, reaching 277,000. The number of employed persons stood at 2,547,000, which was 7,000 fewer than in December 2024. The rise in unemployment was reflected across all age groups.

item.title: Asia tightens travel checks after Nipah virus outbreak in India
item.description: Health authorities across Asia have begun screening air travellers arriving from India after five confirmed cases of the Nipah virus in the country’s eastern state of West Bengal. Thailand, Nepal and Taiwan have moved quickly to introduce preventive measures amid growing concern over the virus’s high fatality rate and epidemic potential. item.title: Amazon cuts 16,000 corporate jobs worldwide
item.description: Amazon will cut 16,000 corporate roles worldwide, marking its second wave of layoffs in three months. The move affects office-based staff, not warehouse or logistics workers. Amazon employs 1.5 million people globally, of whom about 350,000 hold corporate positions. This round follows a cut of 14,000 roles announced in October, bringing the total to 30,000 jobs eliminated since late 2025.

item.title: SDP leader Tuppurainen denies claims of inappropriate conduct
item.description: Tytti Tuppurainen, chair of the Social Democratic Party’s (SDP) parliamentary group, has rejected allegations of inappropriate behaviour towards assistants and MPs, following reports by Finnish media citing multiple anonymous sources. She said the claims were false and damaging and stated she would not step down from her position. Speaking at a press conference at the Parliament on Wednesday, Tuppurainen said the claims published by the Finnish News Agency STT were inaccurate and offensive.

item.title: Orpo visits China as Europe reconsiders its stance on Beijing
item.description: Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo concluded a six-day visit to China on 29 January 2026. The trip included high-level meetings in Beijing and commercial talks involving 20 Finnish companies. Orpo met Chinese President Xi Jinping, Premier Li Qiang, and National People’s Congress Chairman Zhao Leji on 27 January. One day earlier, he held discussions with Commerce Minister Wang Wentao. The agenda included bilateral relations, Ukraine, market access, and EU-China trade balance.

item.title: Private social services wage negotiations collapse
item.description: Wage negotiations in Finland’s private social services sector have ended without agreement after weeks of talks, affecting around 72,000 workers including practical nurses. The talks, held between trade unions and employer representatives, broke down late Wednesday evening. The employee side, led by unions including SuPer, Tehy, Erto, JHL, Talentia and Salli ry, walked out of the negotiations after failing to reach consensus with employer organisation Hyvinvointiala Hali ry.

item.title: Carlyle to acquire Lukoil's overseas business under US sanctions deadline
item.description: Carlyle Group has reached a provisional agreement to acquire the international assets of Russian oil firm Lukoil, following increased pressure from US sanctions introduced in October. The deal, announced by both parties, excludes Lukoil's operations in Kazakhstan and is subject to regulatory approval from the US Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). Lukoil has until 28 February to comply with a US directive requiring the divestment of its overseas assets.

item.title: EU sanctions Iranian officials and designates IRGC a terrorist group
item.description: The European Union has imposed new sanctions on senior Iranian officials and entities, citing human rights abuses and support for Russia’s war in Ukraine. The bloc has also listed Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organisation. The move follows months of internal EU debate and growing international concern over Tehran’s crackdown on protest movements and weapons exports to Russia.

item.title: Ähtäri Zoo to reopen with new structure and investor backing
item.description: Ähtäri Zoo will resume operations under a restructured two-operator model following its closure in October 2025. The plan was announced on 29 January at a local investor meeting in Ähtäri. The model divides responsibilities between two separate entities. Vieraile ja Välität ry, an association of former zoo employees that acquired the animals and facilities after bankruptcy, will remain in charge of animal care, species protection, and educational services.
